title: Basic Electroencephalography
description: This course covers the fundamentals of electroencephalography (EEG). The application of electrodes, basic waveforms, artifacts and introduction to the EEG machine are covered. The course is designed for students enrolled in the Neurodiagnostic Technology Program.
outcomes: Students will be able to identify anatomical landmarks appropriate for clinical practice.
Students will be able to identity basic waveforms and artifacts.
Students will be able to identify normal and abnormal adult EEG recordings.
Students will be able to demonstrate measurement of electrodes sites according to appropriate standards of clinical practice.
objectives: Set up the International 10/20 system to measure and apply the 21 23 standard EEG electrodes on a mannequin head accurately (to within 5mm) and within 45 minutes.
Define and identify the basic EEG rhythms, activity, and artifacts on the recording.
Describe, define and perform the standard EEG activations used in routine recordings.
Define, describe and utilize the major instrument controls such as high and low filters, sensitivity, and calibration.
Describe, list and set up all of the recommended montages used in routine EEG.
Apply electrodes using collodion accurately so as to record EEG activity for 24 hour recordings or for an all-night polysomnogram.
Calibrate an EEG instrument accurately and be able to troubleshoot basic equipment malfunctions.
Describe and perform proper cleaning/disinfection techniques of electrodes and equipment.
content: Appropriate selection for EEG to be done
Electrode Application and Types of Electrodes
Digital EEG (analog/digital conversion and digital filtering)
Electrode and Equipment Care including Electrode Care, Cleaning and Disinfecting
lab: Introduction to EEG Equipment, EEG Program, Amplifier Calibration, Activations and ACNS Guidelines
Utilization of the International 10/20 System for Measurement and Application of the 21 23 Standard EEG Electrodes on Mannequins
Identification on the Recording of Basic EEG Rhythms, Activity and Artifacts
Performance of Standard EEG Activations Used in Routine Recordings
Identification and Utilization of the Major Instrument Controls
Completion of an Accurate Patient History
Application of Electrodes Using Collodion to Record EEG Activity for 24 Hr Recording or an All-Night Polysomnogram
Calibration of EEG Instrument Including Ability to Troubleshoot Basic Equipment Malfunctions
Performance of Proper Cleaning/Disinfection Techniques of Electrodes and Equipment
assignments: Professional journals including Journal of Clinical Neurophysiology and Neurodiagnostic Journal
Skills homework practicing measuring and marking mannequin head
Successfully completely lab practicums for measurement and application of electrodes on mannequin head.
Accurate "PSG Style" collodion application of electrodes with limited recording of EEG activity.
